description: What ecoinvent states about one unit of its own flows, read for the merge (#407). Every value here was a bare `conversion_factor` on a row of `ecoinvent-match-overrides.json` until #407; the numbers are unchanged and each now says what quantity it is, which unit it is in, which releases it was checked against and where it came from. Shared by every ecoinvent release the manifests declare, with `by_release` where a release restated a measurement: crude oil was 42.3 MJ/kg in 3.8 and 43.4 from 3.9.1 on, and 3.8's natural gas is per plain cubic metre where later releases are per standard cubic metre. The coal values come from ecoinvent's EF 3.1 implementation workbook, which states no basis, so they are `calorific-value`; crude oil and natural gas carry `heating value, net` on the exchange itself from 3.9 on and are `net-calorific-value`; uranium is fission energy, never a heat of combustion. Since phase B of #407 the adapter reads the `heating value, net` and `heating value, gross` properties ecoinvent states on its exchanges (crude oil and natural gas from 3.9.1, and some thirty emission flows in 3.12) onto the flows as the vendor's own statements; an entry here names those releases in `stated_by_vendor_in` and states the number only for 3.8, which carries none.

primary_source: ecoinvent's EF 3.1 LCIA Implementation workbook, sheet CFs, category `Resource use, fossils`: the factor on the kilogram or cubic-metre flow, which is 1 MJ/MJ times the energy content; the exchange carries no heating value property
statements.comment: The energy-content conversions the retired tables carried (#141), restated as this project's rows with nothing changed: ecoinvent extracts its fossil energy carriers and sea water in kilograms and EF 3.1 publishes the resources in megajoules (or as its own basis), and the factor is the carrier's energy content -- 9.41 MJ/kg brown coal, 18.01 hard coal, 43.4 crude oil, 36.0 natural gas, 560,000 uranium, and sea water's density pairing. Without these the retirement build landed every one of the rows on a kilogram flow of the right substance and EF's fossil-depletion factors, which live on the energy flows, became unreachable from ecoinvent -- the #33 underestimate by a new road. The numbers are the tables' own, read out of the composed 3.8 table before its retirement. Read off ecoinvent's own LCIA implementation workbooks, one per release: `LCIA Implementation v3.8.xlsx`, `3.9.1`, `3.10.1`, `3.11` and `3.12`, `energy resources: non-renewable` under EF v3.0 and EF v3.1. The characterisation factor for a kilogram flow under an indicator defined per megajoule is the energy content, which is why the workbook answers this question at all. The same number in all five releases' workbooks, so the row's factor needs no release of its own. (#162)

primary_source: ecoinvent's documentation of its natural uranium resource: 560 GJ per kilogram, a gross fission energy content; the same number on every list that ships uranium by mass

primary_source: the density of sea water, 1024.6 kg per cubic metre (1025 as ecoinvent's EF 3.1 implementation rounds it)
statements.comment: One of the energy-content family; the full reasoning is on the family's first row above. (#141) Checked across releases against the three published correspondence tables that ever stated it -- `ecoinvent-3.9.1`, `-3.10.1` and `-3.11` biosphere to EF 3.1 biosphere -- which state the same number in each; 3.12 read 3.11's table and 3.8's was composed. The basis cannot carry a release's revision in any case: it is a density of sea water, a property of the substance and not of any ecoinvent release. (#162)

primary_source: ecoinvent 3.8's EF 3.1 LCIA Implementation workbook, sheet CFs, category `Resource use, fossils`: the factor on the cubic-metre flow, which is 1 MJ/MJ times the energy content
statements.comment: ecoinvent 3.8 ships `Gas, natural, in ground` per cubic metre with no heating value property on the exchange; its implementation workbook counts the cubic metre as 34.5 MJ. From 3.9.1 the exchange is per standard cubic metre and carries `heating value, net` 36 and `heating value, gross` 40 as properties, which the adapter reads onto the flow, so this entry covers 3.8 only and names the later releases as the vendor's to state. ecoinvent revised the number at 3.9 following Meili et al. (2022), so converting a 3.8 inventory with 36.0 would use a heating value that release never had (#162).

primary_source: ecoinvent 3.8's EF 3.1 LCIA Implementation workbook, sheet CFs, category `Resource use, fossils`: the factor on the kilogram flow, which is 1 MJ/MJ times the energy content
statements.comment: ecoinvent 3.8 states no heating value on its `Oil, crude` exchange; its implementation workbook counts the kilogram as 42.3 MJ. From 3.9.1 the exchange carries `heating value, net` 43.4 and `heating value, gross` 46 as properties (Meili et al. 2022, section 5.1), which the adapter reads onto the flow, so this entry covers 3.8 only and names the later releases as the vendor's to state. A 3.8 inventory converted at 43.4 would be 2.6% high (#162).
